ST.reason: The distinctive current task demands are actually supplied in Schuljahrgang 9: graph-area interpretation in the motion context, all three time diagrams, accelerated motion and motions with initial conditions. This supports the actual generalized initial-value and signed-area tasks as a reasonable transfer within the taught domain. The native full real P is separately complete, including every foreign prerequisite and an actual lower acquisition placement. The endpoint is approved for terminal practice, without assigning whole-goal mastery to TV or LAWS.
ST.interpretationBoundary: The plan does not literally spell out the exact reversal at t=2.5 s. Applying its motion-with-initial-conditions, signed speed/acceleration and graph-area framework to the given numbers is the independent pedagogical judgment, not a quoted official task or new official full-atom claim.

HH.reason: Neither the retained Hamburg 2011 p.20 nor the current Hamburg 2024 p.32/41 explicitly supplies the signed graph-area reconstruction from an acceleration protocol with nonzero signed initial velocity, nonzero initial position, a shifted time origin and a reversal. The sources support simple motion diagrams and rest-start motion laws, with the current edition also presenting acceleration as a finite velocity change. This does not itself teach the signed area/initial-value coordination assessed at 20/20 in A. All 66 prerequisites occurring in the generated lower graph is insufficient evidence that these extra demands are supplied. Do not add HH binding or any graph-only coverage.
HH.requiredNextStep: Provide and independently review a bounded lower-stage assessment matching the verified Hamburger supply, or explicitly author and review the missing preparation before an offer. No new exam or bridge authored in this Task 4 review. Do not invent official initial-condition/area claims.

creditedCoverage.reason: a8dc requires LAWS and practically uses signed v-areas, but it does not ask interval means from given position-time data and does not assess both uniform and accelerated law extraction from supplied diagrams. This review approves only the existing credited e4b coverage; prerequisite use is distinct from direct credited whole-goal coverage.

exactSourceWitnesses.interpretation: Rest-start equations; simple s-t/v-t communication and free-fall application are on the same page. No signed area or generalized initial-condition law claim is made. Extraction 3.2-MECH is the author-assigned right-column code; official §3.2 is actually p.23.

Current Mechanik II is J8/9. Same page supplies rest-start equations and acceleration as a change ratio, no signed graph-area law. Current p.44 has J10 throws; p.4 and p.29 distinguish upper-introduction/Abitur material. This review does not import that J10 material into the retained lower source.
Movement diagrams, traffic applications, experiments and mechanical modeling on p.45 supply a real context for positive and negative graph areas.

Same page names uniform motion, mean speed, uniform acceleration, all three time diagrams and experiments. The two new Wissensbestände route sourceSpans had p.45 and are corrected to p.46, retaining their partial mapping.

actualTaskPreparationMatrix.ST: Physics p.45-46 coordinated diagrams and motions with initial conditions; Math function values, linear graphs and quadratic terms at PDF p.43/47/52. Choosing tau=t-2 is an algebraic re-expression of the explicitly given initial condition, not calculus.
actualTaskPreparationMatrix.HH: Source p.20/p.41 only prints rest-start laws. General signed initial-condition coordination is not evidenced as supplied by those source routes.

actualTaskPreparationMatrix.taskDemand: A: a-area as delta-v, signed v-areas, difference between displacement and travelled distance
actualTaskPreparationMatrix.ST: Physics p.45 explicitly supplies graph-area interpretation in motion; p.46 supplies v and a diagrams. Signed velocity before/after zero determines signed displacement; taking magnitudes determines distance. This is reviewed interpretation, not an official verbatim full-goal claim. Triangular areas use lower mathematics.
actualTaskPreparationMatrix.HH: No area interpretation in retained p.20 or current motion modules. General area arithmetic in Mathematics cannot supply the missing physical graph-area relation.

actualTaskPreparationMatrix.taskDemand: A: compare s(4)=7.00 m with provided interval 7.03±0.05 m
actualTaskPreparationMatrix.ST: The task supplies the numerical interval; compare 7.00 with 6.98..7.08. This is basic interval/rational-number use with the native measurement-resolution goal, not new statistical uncertainty propagation. Physics lower experiments and data comparisons support it.
actualTaskPreparationMatrix.HH: This part by itself is accessible; it does not repair the missing initial-value/area preparation.

actualTaskPreparationMatrix.taskDemand: B: negative acceleration, general braking laws, stopping time/distance, physical limit of continued model
actualTaskPreparationMatrix.ST: Initial-condition motions, three diagrams, traffic applications and Newtonian motion in p.45-46. Once v=0, a nonzero constant a changes v and cannot describe permanent rest; no additional mechanics topic or calculus is needed.
actualTaskPreparationMatrix.HH: Simple traffic modeling is source-supported, but the full exact A+B task remains beyond the demonstrated supplied basis.

foreignPreparationReview.judgment: Individually read every foreign prerequisite description and actual lower placement. Natural numbers, rational arithmetic, units, coordinates, areas, expressions, functions and linear graphs suffice. Three canonical mathematics phase labels E do not force upper-stage acquisition: their actual descriptions are function value evaluation, function representations and linear functions, covered in lower Mathematics. Quadratic evaluations and turning points are available in ST year 9 (PDF p.52, printed p.50). No derivative, integral, upper-stage vector algebra or probability is required. The broad foundational prerequisites stay counted without pruning.
